answer: Give each identity a weight that grows only with age and distinct trading partners, not with capital alone. A fresh account is a faint plume with zero say; weight accrues slowly as it transacts with many others, and any single partner counts just once. An attacker who splits funds across clones gains nothing, because no clone inherits the trusted relic of past history. To match one honest agent's voice, every fake identity must trade for months across a wide garden of counterparties, paying fees and waiting. Cloning is cheap; manufacturing that much aged, varied history is slow and costly.
